# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Start with your coaches first, not members.** Sit down with each coach individually (30 mins max) and ask: "What do you actually deliver?" Get specifics—circuit classes, 1-on-1 strength coaching, nutrition guidance, mobility work. Let them define their own offer. This prevents you building a menu that doesn't match reality on the gym floor.

• **Price by outcome, not time.** Don't list "Personal Training - £50/hour." Instead: "6-Week Strength Build (2x weekly, 1-on-1) - £360" or "Drop-In Classes - £12 per session." Members buy results, not duration. Coaches will know what transformation costs them.

• **Create TWO menus simultaneously:** One internal (for coaches showing what's available to sell to members) and one for your website/marketing (what members see). The coach version should include margins, caps, and any upsells. The member version is clean, benefit-focused, no pricing confusion.

• **Build it in a Google Sheet first, not a designer.** Real data beats pretty. Share the draft with 3-4 loyal members and 2 coaches this week. Ask: "Would you buy this? What's missing? What's confusing?" Iterate based on real feedback, then design once you know it works.

• **Bundle ruthlessly.** Don't sell individual services. Create 3-4 tiers (e.g., "The Starter," "The Athlete," "The Transformation") that include class access + coaching + some add-on. Bundles reduce decision paralysis and increase average member value immediately.

# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO BRIEF

## REVENUE — CRITICAL PRIORITY

**•CHURN SPIKE IN MAY (12.8%) IS THE KILLER:** You gained 12 members net April–May but lost 17 to churn in May alone. That's unsustainable and masks real growth. Root cause likely post-relocation friction (new schedule, pricing shock, facility teething). Action: Run retention audit this week — survey lapsed members, audit class timetable fit, check post-move onboarding. Target: drop May-level churn to 5% baseline (your norm Feb–Apr, Jun–Sep). At 154 active members now, a 1% churn improvement = 2–3 retained members = ~£1,500/month recurring.

**• Rev/member collapsed Aug (£105, lowest 8-month point) despite 154 active members — your highest headcount.** This signals either: (a) too many intro/discounted-rate members post-growth, (b) class-card uptake weak, or (c) low ancillary sales. Sept recovered to £129 (+23%) with 171 members. Action: Segment membership tiers in TeamUp now. Identify how many are on introductory pricing and set auto-upgrade dates (e.g. month 3 → full price). Introduce tiered membership: Standard (£25/mth implied from Sept average), Premium (+£8 for off-peak unlimited), Corporate partner block pricing (sell 5-packs to local offices). Target: £135+ rev/member by Nov.

**• Sept momentum is real (+£6k vs Aug, +23% rev/member) on membership growth alone** — but you need to lock in: (a) upsells — retail (water, merchandise, protein), PT sessions (1:1 or small group at £30–50/session), class passes (top-up for corporate/day visitors), (b) new revenue lines — corporate wellness contracts (Belfast tech/finance firms), merchandise (branded kit — 15–20% margin), partner commissions (nutritionist, physio referrals).

---

## EXPENSES — CLEAR PATTERN

**• Last 3 months (Jul–Sep): cash out averaged £23.5k vs. revenue £19.3k = persistent £4k+ monthly burn despite membership growth.** Exclude relocation, but you're overspending. Biggest leaks likely: (1) payroll (studio closure/relocation may have created double-rent or severance), (2) utilities (larger new space in Belfast CBD?), (3) equipment leasing or contractor overheads.
